title: Bearings and Angles of Elevation
seo_title: Precalculus Bearings and Angles of Elevation Worksheets (TEKS P.4E, P.4F)
standard_text: P.4E determine the value of trigonometric ratios of angles and solve problems involving trigonometric ratios in mathematical and real-world problems; P.4F use trigonometry in mathematical and real-world problems, including directional bearing
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on bearings and angles of elevation for Texas TEKS P.4E and P.4F: true and compass bearings, trip components, two-leg trips, back bearings and elevation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bearings are measured clockwise from north.
key_sub: North component d cos β; east component d sin β.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A true bearing is measured clockwise from north, with three digits: 045°. A compass bearing like N 45° E starts at north or south and turns toward east or west.
  • Standard-position angle θ = 90° − bearing.
  • For a trip of distance d on bearing β: north component d cos β, east component d sin β.
  • The angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal; the angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal.

Examples

Example

20 miles on a bearing of 060°

North: 20 cos 60° = 10

East: 20 sin 60° ≈ 17.3

Answer: 10 miles north, 17.3 miles east

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Measuring from the x-axisBearings start at north and go clockwise.
Sine for the north componentNorth uses cosine of the bearing.
The depression angle at the wrong cornerIt equals the elevation angle from the other end.

faq.a: Determine the value of trigonometric ratios of angles and solve problems involving trigonometric ratios in mathematical and real-world problems.
Use trigonometry in mathematical and real-world problems, including directional bearing.

faq.q: Why do bearings use three digits?
faq.a: So 045° and 450 cannot be confused, and all directions look the same.

faq.q: How do I find a back bearing?
faq.a: Add 180° (or subtract it if the bearing is over 180°).

sets.title: Back bearings and angles between bearings

items.q: From a lighthouse, ship P is on a bearing of 035° and ship Q is on a bearing of 220°. What is the angle between the two lines of sight?
items.e: Subtract the bearings: |220° − 35°| = 185° and 360° − that is smaller. 175°.

items.q: A plane flies from town A to town B on a bearing of 050°. On what bearing must it fly to go straight back from B to A?
items.e: The return trip is the opposite direction: add or subtract 180°. 230°.
